name: V-22 Osprey
summary: Tiltrotor that takes off like a helicopter and cruises like a turboprop by rotating its wingtip engine nacelles, flown by the Marines, Air Force special operations and the Navy.

wings: High-mounted straight wing with an engine nacelle at each tip
Huge three-blade proprotors, pointing up for hover or forward for cruise
engines: Two engines inside the tilting wingtip nacelles
Nacelles rotate through 90 degrees between vertical and horizontal
fuselage: Boxy fuselage with sponsons housing retractable tricycle gear
Rear loading ramp under an upswept tail
Refueling probe on the nose; CV-22 has a bulged radar nose; CMV-22B has larger sponsons
tail: H-tail: twin vertical fins at the ends of the horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Two enormous rotors on tilting wingtip nacelles
Twin vertical fins on an H-shaped tail
Wing with no engines except at the tips

confusedWith.howToTell: The Osprey's rotors sit side by side on wingtips and it has an H-tail; the Chinook's rotors are front and rear on a wingless fuselage.
The C-130 has four turboprops on a high wing and a single tall fin; the Osprey has two huge tilting rotors at the wingtips and twin fins.

usCount.source: USMC MV-22B ~290, USAF CV-22B ~50, USN CMV-22B ~45 (FlightGlobal World Air Forces 2025)
